# EXPECTED.md — what the fixtures must contain

This file is written **by hand from `src/`**, not generated by running Stellar.
A machine-generated file would only assert that Stellar agrees with itself; the
point of these fixtures is to state, independently of the dumper, what the
debug info *ought* to say. Line numbers below are the declaration line a
compiler is required to record (`DW_AT_decl_line`), counted from 1 in the file
named beside each entry.

Paths are given relative to `tests/fixtures/`.

## Variants

| File | DWARF | Optimisation | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lib/stellar-fixture-dwarf4-O0.so` | 4 | `-O0` | **primary** |
| `lib/stellar-fixture-dwarf4-O2.so` | 4 | `-O2` | primary, optimised |
| `lib/stellar-fixture-dwarf5-O0.so` | 5 | `-O0` | secondary |
| `lib/stellar-fixture-dwarf5-O2.so` | 5 | `-O2` | secondary, optimised |

All four are ELF64, little-endian, `EM_AARCH64` (`AArch64`), `ET_DYN`, and each
carries `.debug_info`, `.debug_abbrev`, `.debug_str` and `.debug_line`. The
DWARF-5 pair additionally carries `.debug_line_str`, which is where DWARF 5
puts directory and file names; DWARF 4 has no such section and keeps its names
in `.debug_str`.

The two units in every variant are, in this order, `body.cpp` then `player.cpp`.

### Comp dir

`-ffile-prefix-map` rewrites the absolute checkout path, so in all four
libraries:

    DW_AT_comp_dir  ("/stellar-fixtures/src")
    DW_AT_name      ("Classes/Player/hitboxes/body.cpp")   [unit 0]
    DW_AT_name      ("Classes/Player/player.cpp")           [unit 1]

A dumper must therefore resolve `DW_AT_name` against `DW_AT_comp_dir`; neither
path exists on the machine running the test.

## Types

`DW_TAG_namespace` `game` wraps every type below in all four libraries.

### `game::Entity` — base class
Declared `src/Classes/Player/hitboxes/body.h:17`.

| Property | Value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `DW_AT_byte_size` | `0x10` (16) | vptr 8 + `float` 4, padded to pointer alignment |
| base class | none | root of the hierarchy |
| members | `health_` at `+0x08`, `DW_AT_byte_size 0x04` | `float`, `protected` |
| methods | `~Entity`, `update`, `describe` | see below |

`DW_AT_byte_size` is 16 even though only 12 bytes are described by real members:
the vtable pointer occupies bytes 0–7. Clang *does* describe it, as a
`DW_TAG_member` named `_vptr$Entity` with `DW_AT_data_member_location 0x00` and
`DW_AT_artificial (true)` — so it is present in the DIE tree, and a dumper must
skip it by name or by `DW_AT_artificial` rather than by assuming the first
member is a real one. `health_` then follows at `+0x08`.

### `game::Hitbox` — the struct with known offsets
Declared `src/Classes/Player/hitboxes/body.h:30`. `sizeof` 16, `alignof` 4.

| Member | Type | Offset | Decl line |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x` | `float` | `0x00` | `body.h:31` |
| `y` | `float` | `0x04` | `body.h:32` |
| `half_w` | `float` | `0x08` | `body.h:33` |
| `half_h` | `float` | `0x0c` | `body.h:34` |

These offsets are fixed by the AArch64 AAPCS64 rules and are identical in all
four variants. They are the one place in this fixture where a value can be
asserted without consulting debug info at all.

### `game::Body` — derives from `Entity`
Declared `src/Classes/Player/hitboxes/body.h:38`.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| `DW_AT_byte_size` | `0x20` (32) |
| base class | `game::Entity` at `DW_AT_data_member_location 0x00` |
| `hitbox_` (`game::Hitbox`) | `DW_AT_data_member_location 0x0c` (12) |
| `shape_` (`game::Body::Shape`) | `DW_AT_data_member_location 0x1c` (28) |

`hitbox_` starts at 12, not 16: `Entity` contributes vptr (8) plus
`health_` (4), so the base subobject is 12 bytes and the derived members follow
immediately. Only the base's `DW_AT_byte_size` of 16 forces the alignment
padding. Any dumper that computes derived-member offsets as
`base_byte_size + accumulated` lands `hitbox_` at 16 instead of 12.

`instances_` is a static data member: `DW_TAG_member` with `DW_AT_external true`
at `body.h:52`, plus a separate `DW_TAG_variable` for the definition.

`game::Body::Shape` is a scoped enumerator type (`enum class`) declared at
`body.h:57`. It is a real `DW_TAG_enumeration_type` carrying
`DW_AT_enum_class (true)` and `DW_AT_byte_size 0x04`, with three
`DW_TAG_enumerator` children:

| Enumerator | `DW_AT_const_value` | Decl line |
|---|---|---|
| `kCircle` | `0` | `body.h:58` |
| `kBox` | `1` | `body.h:59` |
| `kCapsule` | `2` | `body.h:60` |

The `DW_AT_enum_class` flag is the only thing distinguishing this from an
unscoped enum: the enumerator names have no class prefix in DWARF, so a dumper
must read `DW_AT_enum_class` to decide whether to print `Shape.kCircle` or
`kCircle`, and cannot infer it from the names.

### `game::Player`
Declared `src/Classes/Player/player.h:18`. Members: `body_` (`game::Body`) at
`+0x00` (decl line `player.h:27`), `score_` (`int`) at `+0x20` (decl line
`player.h:28`). Three-level containment: `Player` → `Body` → `Entity`.

## Functions

Every function below is declared in a header and defined in a `.cpp`; both
declaration and definition appear in the DWARF, and the *definition* is what
carries the code range.

| Function | Declared | Defined | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `game::Entity::~Entity` | `body.h:19` | `body.cpp:10` | virtual, `= default` |
| `game::Entity::update(float)` | `body.h:20` | `body.cpp:12` | **virtual** |
| `game::Entity::describe() const` | `body.h:23` | `body.cpp:14` | **non-virtual**, empty body |
| `game::Body::Body` | `body.h:40` | `body.cpp:19` | constructor |
| `game::Body::~Body` | `body.h:41` | `body.cpp:25` | `override`, `= default` |
| `game::Body::update(float)` | `body.h:44` | `body.cpp:27` | virtual **override** |
| `game::Body::radius() const` | `body.h:47` | `body.cpp:35` | non-virtual |
| `game::Body::set_hitbox(Hitbox const&)` | `body.h:49` | `body.cpp:37` | by const reference |
| `game::Body::instance_count()` | `body.h:55` | `body.cpp:39` | **static** member function |
| `game::Body::shape() const` | `body.h:63` | `body.cpp:41` | returns the scoped enum |
| `game::Player::Player` | `player.h:20` | `player.cpp:11` | constructor |
| `game::Player::tick(float)` | `player.h:22` | `player.cpp:13` | calls `Body::update` |
| `game::Player::score() const` | `player.h:24` | `player.cpp:18` | getter |

Both vtable symbols are present in all four libraries: `_ZTVN4game6EntityE`
and `_ZTVN4game4BodyE`.

### Virtual vs non-virtual

`Entity::update` and `Body::update` are virtual; `Entity::describe` and
`Body::radius` are not. `describe` is never overridden, so it appears in the
DIE tree of every type exactly once, as a plain `DW_TAG_subprogram` with no
`DW_AT_vtable_elem_location`. `Body::update` is an override of
`Entity::update`, so both classes name a subprogram called `update` — a dumper
that keys methods on the unqualified name alone will conflate
`Entity::update` and `Body::update` unless it also compares
`DW_AT_containing_type`.

### `game::clamp_value<int>` — the template, instantiated once
Defined `src/Classes/Player/player.h:12`–`15`, called once at `player.cpp:11`.

    DW_AT_linkage_name  ("_ZN4game11clamp_valueIiEET_S1_")
    DW_AT_name          ("clamp_value<int>")
    DW_AT_decl_file     (".../Classes/Player/player.h")
    DW_AT_decl_line     (13)

Exactly **one** instantiation exists, because the only call in the whole project
is the explicit `clamp_value<int>(0)` in `Player::Player`. The DIE's name is the
*substituted* name `clamp_value<int>`, not the template parameter spelling —
a dumper that reports `clamp_value` loses the type argument, and one that
reports `clamp_value<T>` is reporting text the DWARF does not contain.

At `-O2` this instantiation may be fully inlined into `Player::Player` and so
have no out-of-line copy; it is present as a standalone `DW_TAG_subprogram` with
a code range in the `-O0` variants.

### `game::clampf` — the function that is only ever inlined
Defined `src/Classes/Util/math.h:14`–`18` (header-only, `inline`), called once
at `src/Classes/Player/hitboxes/body.cpp:32`.

| Variant | Expected encoding |
|---|---|
| `-O0` | `DW_TAG_subprogram` **with** `DW_AT_low_pc`/`DW_AT_high_pc` — an out-of-line copy was emitted |
| `-O2` | `DW_TAG_subprogram` with **`DW_AT_inline (DW_INL_inlined)` and no code range**, plus a `DW_TAG_inlined_subroutine` child at the call site carrying `DW_AT_call_file .../body.cpp`, `DW_AT_call_line 32` |

`DW_AT_decl_file` is `.../Classes/Util/math.h` and `DW_AT_decl_line` is 14 in
both cases. This pair is the fixture's reason for existing: a function that is
present in the debug info but has no address is **not** a parse failure, and one
that is only ever inlined must not be reported as a missing method.

## Variables

| Name | Type | Defined | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `game::Body::instances_` | `int` | `body.cpp:8` | static member; declared `body.h:52`. `DW_AT_external true`, `DW_AT_byte_size 0x04` |
| `game::player_registry_token` | `int` | `player.cpp:9` | the one **global**; `DW_AT_external true`, `DW_AT_byte_size 0x04` |

`player_registry_token` is initialised to `0x5354454c` in the source. DWARF
gives it a `DW_AT_location` expression, not the constant value: the initialiser
lives in `.data`, and a dumper that emits `0x5354454c` as the variable's value
has invented data it did not read from debug info. Reading the *initial* value
is out of scope for DWARF and belongs to `.data`, not to this fixture.

Both variables live in `.data` and are `DW_TAG_variable` children of the `game`
namespace, not of any class scope — except `instances_`, which also has the
in-class `DW_TAG_member` declaration noted above.
